html:
SMTO-TSK-0009 — This run is busy, so its settings can't change yet

GUID: c9a6b606-bea8-42ea-90b0-02b8739341af
Slug: run-settings-busy
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The Agent is in the middle of working on this run. SMTO only changes a run's settings at a safe pause point, so it refused the change instead of interrupting the work. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Pause after current action on the running task, or wait until the reply shows the task has finished or is waiting for you. SMTO only changes a run's settings while the Agent isn't in the middle of a step.
  2. When the task shows Paused, reload the page or reopen the conversation so the settings panel shows the run's current state. The panel then reflects the paused run, so your change is made against what's really there.
  3. Make the setting change again, then select Resume if you want the task to carry on. Once the run is paused, the change is safe to make and applies when it continues.

What success looks like

  • The setting saves without this message and the run continues with the new setting after you resume it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't click the change over and over while the task is running; it will keep being refused until the run pauses.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The server could not take the run's exclusive claim because the run is executing (or has pending work), so a run-scoped settings edit, control action or compaction was refused until a safe idle point.

What this means

  • An exclusive run claim cannot be acquired, an execution owner is active, or compaction sees running/pending work at its idle-only boundary. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • An exclusive run claim cannot be acquired, an execution owner is active, or compaction sees running/pending work at its idle-only boundary.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current ownership, pending operations and action-specific availability; a failed claim alone does not identify a stuck worker.

How to fix it

  • The run is held by an active execution owner (store.is_owned, or store.claim_run could not take the exclusive claim), or compaction found pending or running work. Pause the run or wait for its current step to settle, refresh the run state, and apply the edit once the run is idle; do not loop the request while the owner is active.
  • Wait for the current owner or use supported Pause when available, then refresh and apply the action only at its allowed idle boundary.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The existing owner settles and the supported action acquires its ordinary idle boundary.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
